messages:
incident-bot: [PAGER] Sev2 - SmartRouting fallback surge. Observed large increase in cross-region fallbacks and model-variant mismatches in eu-west-1. Metric alert: fallback_rate=38% -> robby-small, error_5xx spike. Pager: jamie

jamie: ack, I'm on. Pulling routing logs + recent routing policy changes. Paging oliver.

oliver: on it — checking policy DB and the last rollout. I see a policy change at +09:09 that adjusted fallback weights and enabled variant_alias 'v2-beta' as valid fallback in eu-west-1.

jamie: that sounds suspicious. who applied that change?

oliver: looks like a manual change via console by mike at 09:08:22. command: `rctl policy update --id sr-983 --set fallback.alias=v2-beta`

mike: yep that was me — I applied a quick change to move traffic off a degraded instance group. I didn't realize v2-beta wasn't globally compatible. sorry.

jamie: okay. we are seeing routing loop behavior: requests routed to eu-west->fallback to us-east because variant mismatch -> smart-routing detects unavailable variant and retries -> variants bounce between regions. customers seeing elevated latency and some 5xx.

oliver: logs snippet:
```
2026-03-15T09:12:40Z router[pid=22]: route request id=abc123 region=eu-west-1 model=robby v=stable -> fallback to us-east-1 variant=v2-beta
2026-03-15T09:12:41Z router[pid=22]: fallback check failed: variant v2-beta incompatible schema -> escalate to controller
2026-03-15T09:12:41Z controller[pid=6]: override: force-region us-east-1 applied by jamie
2026-03-15T09:12:42Z router[pid=22]: reconcile detected: policy mismatch, re-evaluating route -> sends back to eu-west-1
```

jamie: I tried a manual force-region to move traffic out of eu-west-1 while infra team drains nodes: `/infra override force-region --from eu-west-1 --to us-east-1 --reason "drain eu-west nodes"`

mike: that explains the `force-region` entries. manual override + incompatible fallback alias = bouncing.

sara: paging in — taking lead from here. jamie hand off to me. jamie: what exactly did you change with the force? full global force or per-customer?

jamie: global, I was trying to avoid customers hitting the draining hosts. I can unwind but want to coordinate.

oliver: immediate mitigation options: 1) remove the manual force-region override so routing returns to policy (risk: requests hit drained nodes) 2) pin model variants to v2-stable globally (risk: some traffic might fail if stable isn't available in target region) 3) revert the policy change that set fallback alias to v2-beta.

sara: priority = minimize customer 5xx and latency. Suggest revert fallback alias change first (low risk), then remove force-region after routing stabilizes.

mike: reverting RBAC'd `policy update` now. running `rctl policy update --id sr-983 --unset fallback.alias`

deploy-bot: deploy started by mike — policy-update/sr-983 revert in progress (job id bj-4421).

10s later...

oliver: revert completed per logs. fallback.alias removed. I see initial dip in fallback_rate from 38% -> 22%.

sara: good. jamie — can you start unwinding the force-region? do it carefully: `infra override status` then `infra override unwind --id <override-id> --grace 60s` so draining continues for current requests but new routing isn't forced.

jamie: running unwind now. command: ```
$ infra override unwind --id ov-773 --grace 60
unwind started: ov-773 -> will complete at 09:21:40Z
```

jamie: unwind completed. routing reconciliation started, controller reports no active manual overrides.

oliver: metrics look much better. fallback_rate down to 4%, error_5xx back to baseline. latency 95p reduced from 620ms -> 210ms.

sara: handoff note: I'll keep monitoring for 20m then hand back to jamie. please capture the exact sequence for postmortem.

mike: copying the exact commands I ran to the thread for audit: `rctl policy update --id sr-983 --set fallback.alias=v2-beta` then `rctl policy update --id sr-983 --unset fallback.alias` + job ids.

jamie: customer-impact quick summary: several enterprise tenants in eu-west saw increased p95 and some 502s between 09:12 and 09:20. No data exfiltration or model output corruption observed. Support notified.

sara: action items assigned:
- mike: document the intent behind the policy change + add a gating check to prevent non-global-compatible alias usage (due EOD)
- oliver: add a reconciliation cooldown to auto-detect force-region + alias mismatch and surface a blocking alert (due next week)
- jamie: write incident timeline and hand to postmortem board (due tomorrow)

jamie: marking as resolved in pager. will follow-up with a short postmortem. thanks all :thumbsup:
